text:
Maria Alvarez (support): FYI customer JG reporting a spike in latency and 401s after a policy change. They said requests that should be pinned to eu-west are hitting apac1 instead. Logs + sample request below. Can someone take a look?

JG (customer): We're seeing ~800ms p95 and a bunch of 401s since ~15:02 UTC. This started right after we updated our routing policy in the console. Please advise, this is impacting checkout.

Maria Alvarez (support): Repro steps customer sent: 1) call /v1/generate with header X-Routing-Policy: 0xabc 2) expect region eu-west 3) see route decision header X-Selected-Region: apac1 and auth failures. Sample curl: 

```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Customer: jg" -H "X-Routing-Policy: 0xabc" 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Maria Alvarez (support): Important snippet from route decision log (redacted):

```json
{"req_id":"req-42","policy_id":"0xabc","policy_applied_by":"ui-user@maria","policy_payload":"{...}","selected_region":"apac1","reason":"priority_index:1"}
```

Kevin Liu (eng-infra): Thanks Maria. I pulled the policy 0xabc from the admin API and it shows an array for failover.targets that looks correct on first glance, but the UI commit log shows a transient re-order op right before apply. Suspect a front-end sort vs back-end expectation mismatch.

Ana Patel (eng-runtime): Noted. There's a codepath in routing that expects explicit priority order; if the client submits a JSON where targets is an object rather than an array we normalize it which can change ordering. If console started sending stringified keys (old->new) this could flip. Also sticky cookie TTL + affinity can keep a session pinned to the old region after a swap.

sre-oncall: I can reproduce locally: apply policy payload from the customer and hit the endpoint in a loop. After two requests I see X-Selected-Region: apac1 even though the first response picked eu-west. Looks like a priority flip + cached affinity.

Kevin Liu (eng-infra): Can you paste the exact policy payload you fetched, Maria? Also we need tracer for one failing request (headers + x-request-id). Asking customer for a failing request id.

Maria Alvarez (support): Pasted sanitized policy fragment: 

```json
{"failover": {"targets": ["eu-west", "eu-central", "apac1"], "weights": [0.6, 0.4, 0.0], "sticky": true}}
```

Maria Alvarez (support): Customer sent the failing request-id: req-42 (in logs above). They included an auth token — not sharing — but they report 401s when the request hits apac1 (their token is region-scoped).

Ana Patel (eng-runtime): Ah — weights contain 0.0 for apac1 but selected_region shows apac1 with reason priority_index:1. If the weights array misaligned with targets array (index shift) that would explain it — apac1 might have been moved into index 1 during normalization. We need to confirm whether the UI accidentally sent weights in a different order than targets.

Kevin Liu (eng-infra): Quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily flip sticky=false for that policy (evicts affinity) 2) set explicit integer weights (1/0) to avoid float ordering issues 3) rollback to previous policy commit. Which does customer want?

JG (customer): Please flip sticky off immediately if that's fastest. We can then apply a corrected policy. Billing is spiking because of egress to apac.

Maria Alvarez (support): Done — I created a rollback patch and disabled sticky on policy 0xabc via admin API. Deploy-bot shows the change applied.

deploy-bot: policy 0xabc updated by maria.alvarez at 2812345702 (sticky:false, rollback_to: 0xabb) :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: After the change, I retried the curl loop — now X-Selected-Region respects eu-west. No more 401s in the short repro window. Customer please confirm.

JG (customer): Confirmed — requests are back to eu-west and latency is normal again. Thanks.

Ana Patel (eng-runtime): Root cause plan: I will add defensive validation that enforces targets and weights are zipped on server-side (reject or normalize with warning) and ensure console sends an array for targets. Also will add a migration test for sticky cookie eviction on policy change.

Kevin Liu (eng-infra): I'll follow up with a rollback-safe UI change to ensure the console never serializes the policy as a map. Also adding a quick healthcheck to alert if selected_region != pinned_region for >1% of requests per minute.

Maria Alvarez (support): Filing an incident for billing spike and customer impact, tagging CS and billing to reconcile egress costs.

sre-oncall: Saving traces for req-42 and a few other failing reqs to /internal/traces/2812345678/; moving to postmortem channel after we validate fix.

Ana Patel (eng-runtime): ETA for server-side validation PR: 3-4 hours to staging, 24h for safe rollout (will canary). I'll include a repro unit test using the customer's payload.

Kevin Liu (eng-infra): I'll coordinate with infra to add the alert mentioned above and a one-time billing alert rule so finance notices the unusual egress.

Maria Alvarez (support): Closing loop with customer now. Thanks team. :heart:

JG (customer): Appreciate the fast response.
